title: The Walnut-Tree
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Walnut-tree, which grew by the roadside, bore every year a plentiful crop of nuts. Every one who passed by pelted its branches with sticks and stones, in order to bring down the fruit, and the tree suffered severely. "It is hard," it cried, "that the very persons who enjoy my fruit should thus reward me with insults and blows."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did the Walnut-tree grow?
According to the passage, what did the tree bear every year?
According to the passage, what did passers-by do to the tree's branches?
options: Pelted them with sticks and stones

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did people throw sticks and stones at the tree?
According to the passage, what does the tree call it "hard" that people do?
options: Reward it with insults and blows for the very fruit they enjoy

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "pelted" mean in "pelted its branches with sticks and stones"?
As the passage uses it, what does "plentiful" mean in "a plentiful crop of nuts"?
Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Trees should be planted far from any road
Those who provide a benefit are sometimes repaid with harm rather than gratitude
Fruit is only worth having if it is easy to gather
People always treat generosity with kindness in return

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the tree suffer as a result of being pelted?
According to the passage, what exact word introduces the tree's complaint?
According to the passage, who does the tree say rewards it with insults and blows?
options: Strangers who never come near it
The very persons who enjoy its fruit
Animals that live in its branches

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "severely" mean in "the tree suffered severely"?
Based on the passage, why is the tree's complaint ironic?
options: The people who harm it are the same ones who benefit from its fruit
The tree actually enjoys being pelted
The tree never produces any fruit at all
The people who pelt it never eat the nuts

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Walnut-tree stops bearing fruit after being struck too often
A Walnut-tree that bears plentiful fruit is struck and harmed each year by the very people who gather that fruit
A Walnut-tree is cut down by travelers along the road
A Walnut-tree is protected from harm by a passing traveler
